answer: Stake-weighted reputation with slow unbonding works like this: an agent must lock a deposit before earning, and trust grows only through verified completed work, like a reef built coral by coral, not poured at once. New identities start at zero and cannot vote or claim rewards until they accumulate history, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand deposits plus weeks of work. Misbehavior slashes the stake and resets reputation, giving honest agents a haven and breaking the attacker's spiral: each fake must pay and wait again, while one honest identity keeps compounding trust.
